narration: Buy two get one free sounds like a win. But seventy-three percent of shoppers only wanted one item — and that 'free' product just cost you thirty-four bucks.
visual: Large BOGO price tag springs down from top. Three product boxes slide in from sides. Third box gets a glowing FREE badge. Subtext: '73% only wanted 1 item'.

narration: Here's why. Your brain literally can't process the word 'free' rationally. The moment you see it, the pain of paying shuts off completely — and retailers flip that switch on purpose.
visual: Brain SVG on light background. Giant glowing orange 'FREE' text pulses. A 'pain of paying' meter bar drains to zero as the word FREE appears.

narration: Here's the actual math. Three items at fourteen dollars each is forty-two dollars total. You 'saved' fourteen — but spent twenty-eight more than you ever planned to.
visual: Three price tags appear one by one on dark background. Total $42 appears. Green 'Saved $14' vs red 'Overspent $28' side by side — overspent value pops to full scale.

narration: And stores love it. Retailers running BOGO deals profit twenty-five to forty percent more per transaction. They're not being generous — they're engineering your cart size.
visual: Store front SVG on light background. Two-bar chart: regular sale bar vs BOGO bar — BOGO bar towers over the other. '+40%' label pops above it.

narration: The average shopper falls for four of these a month. At thirty-four dollars each, that's an extra hundred-thirty-six every month — over seventeen hundred dollars a year.
visual: Four shopping bags pop in one by one. Monthly counter climbs to $136. Annual counter races up to $1,700 in red, oversized text.

narration: Before you grab that extra item, ask yourself: would I buy this at full price? If the answer's no — walk away. That's seventeen hundred dollars back in your pocket every year.
visual: Light background. Question text fades in. Big red NO button pops. Arrow pointing to piggy bank. Final text: 'That's $1,700 back' in large orange type.
